You will not get good at Claude if you don't have 5 seconds to re-learn the basics (again & again).

I taught my mom Claude the other day; she's a retired pharmacist. These are the 7 lessons we went through:

LESSON 1: There is not one Claude, but four.

Starting from the two worst models that you should NOT use even if they are free- Haiku 4.5 & Sonnet 5. I would rather use free ChatGPT. But you can use them for spelling checks.

Start any complex task with Fable 5.1 for the first 2 initial prompts to figure out the final outcome.

Switch to Opus-5 (High) mid-chat to do the task and give you the outcome.

LESSON 2: Paste this prompt to start any new chat.

“I need [task] for [goal]. I will know it worked when [target]. Ask me questions first, using the AskUserQuestion tool.”

Claude will give you a clickable form. Always write more context in the "something else" option. Don't be lazy.

LESSON 3: You can't escape AI writing patterns.

But you can make it less obvious by avoiding the giveaways of AI. I made a Claude Skill to get simplified text out of Claude. I will send it directly to your inbox: https://t.co/rFXoSKBTCL

LESSON 4: You never tried this in Claude

Research mode: It plans & reads sources to give you analyst reports.
Claude Artifacts: You can build mini functional apps and then share them publicly with a link.
HTML image: Claude is not built to make images. But if you ask it to make an image in HTML format. It'll never get the text wrong on the images.
Incognito mode: If you don't want the memory to poison a specific chat. Go to the top right. And use it when you want a genuinely new idea.
Interactive chart: Upload a CSV, ask for an interactive chart. I use this all the time.

LESSON 5: Don't make your Claude dumber.

The only habit I'd force you to adopt is to start a new chat after sending 40 prompts in the old chat. It'll hallucinate & won't give you what you want.

Every follow-up prompt stacks on top of the full chat history. Claude re-reads all of it every turn. Instead: click “Restart the conversation from here” on a previous message.

LESSON 6: These 5 behaviours are a no-go

✦ Do not use Fable 5 for the tasks that Opus 5 can perform. You will waste (a lot) of tokens.
✦ Use Projects (with files) for repeated tasks. New chats for creative ideas. Incognito mode for no-context chats.
✦ Turn long (most used) prompts into Claude Skills.
✦ Don't prompt with adjectives. Paste bad writing and say: never write like this.
✦ Don't focus on trying everything new launched. If something works, stick to it.

LESSON 7: Spread your work across the day

Claude uses a rolling 5-hour window. So I usually send something right when I arrive at the office and then early + late afternoon. So about 3 sessions. 2 is enough.

Imagine if a company had access to your name, biometrics, phone, email, address, IDs, IP, cookies, mobile ad IDs, browsing, searches, keystrokes, demographics, card data, photos, audio, and video.

This isn’t theory, it’s Walmart.

Walmart tracks you in the store and online.

In the store: • Cameras and “automated technologies” inside and on the property for checkout, theft, and store layout • Wi-Fi and Bluetooth can locate your phone so the app can push nearby products and navigate you • GPS for store finder and grocery pickup • License plate readers (ALPRs) where legal — kept 60 days — for security, theft, parking, safety • Phone number at bakery, Auto Care, etc. can be tied to your Walmart account and used for ads and recommendations
Cash + no app + no Wi-Fi + no account cuts the digital link. It does not turn off cameras or plate readers.

Online they stitch it together with cookies, pixels, partners, and (if you opt in) VIZIO data. 

Ads follow you. Purchase history can meet browsing history.

Terms of Use pile on: • Your wireless carrier may hand over number, name, address, email, and device IDs (IMSI/IMEI) for “identity and fraud” • Chatbot/AI inputs are not confidential. What you type, plus purchase history and personal info, can train their models • Content you post is a perpetual, royalty-free license to Walmart • They can monitor how you use the sites • Mandatory individual arbitration. No class action. 

Using the app, a Walmart site, or walking in under those systems is acceptance. Location/Bluetooth off, ad-preference opt-outs, and skipping the phone pad at checkout reduce it. They do not stop the cameras.

All this and you give Walmart a pass for breaches. You indemnify Walmart for misuse or ToS breaches.

Among the uses: profile for order fulfillment, customer service, security/fraud, store operations, recommendations (including AR try-on), targeted ads, analytics, and AI training.

Sources: Walmart Customer Privacy Notice (updated Aug 20, 2026) and Walmart Terms of Use (June 23, 2026). Read them yourself before you tap “agree.”

Before @axisrobotics had funding, a token, or a main product, it started with a simple experiment.

The goal was to:

Browser → Data → Model → Real Robot

Could people control a virtual robot arm, create useful training data, and use that data to teach a real robot?

The task was simple:

Water a virtual rose.

Anyone could join, even without robotics experience.

The results:

→ 15,000+ participants
→ 85,000+ training sessions
→ Data used to train a robot model

Then came the real test.

The trained model was deployed on a real Franka robot arm.

The result:

Virtual rose → Training data → Real robot → Real rose

And it worked.

All in just five days.

A second experiment went even further:

→ 27 tasks
→ 18,000+ participants
→ 100,000+ valid trajectories

To me, this is where the Axis story really begins.

They did not try to solve every robotics problem at once.

They started with one simple question:

Can crowdsourced data actually teach robots?

The rose experiment showed that it can.

Now Axis is taking that same idea toward much bigger Physical AI problems.
